title: The Insane Story Behind the Bugatti Chiron

scenes.text: The Bugatti Chiron exists because of a toy in a souvenir shop, a sketch on an envelope, and a brand that had died more than once. The company behind it lost a founder's son in a crash, went bankrupt in Italy, and was bought for its name alone. This is the insane story behind the Bugatti Chiron.
scenes.caption: THE STORY BEHIND THE CHIRON

scenes.text: It is a story with a Monaco racing driver, a Formula One champion buying a car without asking for a discount, a former Formula One driver breaking a record without a helmet, and a car that ended up being sold by a company Volkswagen no longer owns.
scenes.caption: MONACO, F1, AND A TOY

scenes.text: Every fact in this video comes from a published source, listed in the description. And to understand the Chiron, we have to go back more than one hundred years, to a small town in Alsace.
scenes.caption: EVERY FACT IS SOURCED

scenes.text: Here is the first twist. When Bugatti was born, its home town was not in France. It was in Germany.
scenes.caption: IT WAS NOT IN FRANCE

scenes.text: Ettore Bugatti was born in Milan, Italy. In nineteen oh nine he founded his car company in Molsheim, in Alsace, which at that time was part of the German Empire. After the First World War, Alsace became part of France, and Bugatti became one of the great names of French motoring.
scenes.caption: ETTORE BUGATTI, 1909

scenes.text: Bugatti built cars that were light, beautiful, and fast. The Type thirty-five became one of the most successful racing cars of its era. Bugattis won the Targa Florio road race in Sicily every year from nineteen twenty-five to nineteen twenty-nine.
scenes.caption: THE TYPE 35

scenes.text: One of the drivers who made those cars famous was Louis Chiron. He was born in Monte Carlo on the third of August, eighteen ninety-nine. He started racing in nineteen twenty-three in a second-hand Bugatti Brescia, and in nineteen twenty-eight he became a Bugatti factory driver.
scenes.caption: LOUIS CHIRON, MONACO

scenes.text: Chiron won the Italian Grand Prix in nineteen twenty-eight, the German Grand Prix in nineteen twenty-nine, the Belgian Grand Prix in nineteen thirty, and in nineteen thirty-one he won both the French Grand Prix and his home race, the Monaco Grand Prix. Wikipedia notes that he had the most podium finishes of any driver in Bugattis.
scenes.caption: MONACO GP WINNER, 1931

scenes.text: And here is a twist. Chiron raced for an incredibly long time. In nineteen fifty-five, at fifty-five years old, he started the Monaco Grand Prix and finished sixth. He is still the oldest driver to start a Formula One race. And he was the only driver from Monaco to win the Monaco Grand Prix until Charles Leclerc did it in twenty twenty-four.
scenes.caption: OLDEST F1 STARTER: 55

scenes.text: Today a statue of Louis Chiron stands at the Monaco circuit, and one corner is named after him. So when Bugatti picked his name for its new hypercar, it was choosing the driver who, more than anyone, connected Bugatti with winning.
scenes.caption: A CORNER IN HIS NAME

scenes.text: In the late nineteen thirties, Ettore's son Jean Bugatti was the rising star of the company. He developed the chassis of the Type fifty-seven C, and a streamlined race version known as the Tank was built for Le Mans.
scenes.caption: JEAN BUGATTI

scenes.text: On the eighteenth of June nineteen thirty-nine, a Type fifty-seven C Tank won the twenty-four hours of Le Mans. The drivers were Jean-Pierre Wimille and Pierre Veyron. According to Bugatti, they covered three thousand three hundred fifty-four kilometers at an average of about one hundred thirty-nine kilometers per hour, and the mechanics never had to open the hood.
scenes.caption: LE MANS WINNERS, 1939

scenes.text: Yes, that Veyron. Pierre Veyron, the co-winner of that race, is the man the Bugatti Veyron was named after, decades later. The two hypercars of the modern Bugatti era carry the names of two of its racing drivers.
scenes.caption: THE REAL VEYRON

scenes.text: But less than two months after that victory, the story turned dark. On the eleventh of August nineteen thirty-nine, Jean Bugatti died while testing a Type fifty-seven tank-bodied race car near the Molsheim factory. He was the heir to the company.
scenes.caption: AUGUST 11, 1939

scenes.text: Weeks later, the Second World War began. The war left the Molsheim factory in ruins, and the company lost control of the property. Ettore Bugatti died on the twenty-first of August, nineteen forty-seven. The golden age of Bugatti was over.
scenes.caption: WAR AND RUIN

scenes.text: In nineteen sixty-three, what remained of the company was sold to Hispano-Suiza, mainly for its aircraft parts business. For years, the name Bugatti meant old masterpieces in museums and auctions, not new cars.
scenes.caption: A NAME IN MUSEUMS

scenes.text: Then came the first revival. In nineteen eighty-seven, Italian entrepreneur Romano Artioli acquired the Bugatti brand and founded Bugatti Automobili S p A. He built a new factory in Campogalliano, in Italy, on a large site near Ferrari, Maserati, and Lamborghini. People called it the Blue Factory.
scenes.caption: THE BLUE FACTORY

scenes.text: The result was the E B one ten, presented in Paris on the fifteenth of September nineteen ninety-one, the day Ettore Bugatti would have turned one hundred ten. It had a three point five liter V12 with four turbochargers, all-wheel drive, and, according to Bugatti, the first series-production carbon chassis. Top speed was over three hundred fifty-one kilometers per hour.
scenes.caption: EB110, 1991

scenes.text: The Blue Factory itself was a statement. Bugatti says it stood on a site of about two hundred forty thousand square meters, and it was designed by Artioli's cousin, Giampaolo Benedini, who also reworked the first design of the E B one ten. It was meant to be the most modern supercar plant of its time, and it sat in the heart of Italy's supercar valley.
scenes.caption: 240,000 SQUARE METERS

scenes.text: Artioli also had bigger plans. Bugatti was developing the E B one twelve, a super saloon with a six liter V12 and a carbon chassis. It was almost finished, but it never launched. If the company had survived, Bugatti might have become a maker of fast luxury sedans, not hypercars.
scenes.caption: THE EB112 THAT NEVER LAUNCHED

scenes.text: And here is a great detail. After testing the E B one ten against rivals, Formula One champion Michael Schumacher bought a yellow Super Sport. According to Bugatti, he did it without even asking for a discount.
scenes.caption: SCHUMACHER'S BUGATTI

scenes.text: But the business did not survive. Artioli also invested in Lotus, which added to the company's debts. Only about one hundred twenty-eight E B one tens were built. Bugatti Automobili filed for bankruptcy on the twenty-third of September nineteen ninety-five. Bugatti says Artioli paid his two hundred twenty employees until the last day.
scenes.caption: BANKRUPT, 1995

scenes.text: Twist number two. The Bugatti brand had now died twice. Once after the war, and once in Italy. When Volkswagen came looking, there was no factory to buy and no product line. There was only a name.
scenes.caption: THE BRAND DIED TWICE

scenes.text: This is where Ferdinand Piech enters the story. He was the engineer who ran the Volkswagen Group, and the grandson of Ferdinand Porsche. According to Top Gear, his son Gregor saw a toy Bugatti Type fifty-seven S C Atlantic in a souvenir shop in Majorca. Piech bought two, one for his son, and one for the Volkswagen executive board.
scenes.caption: A TOY IN MAJORCA

scenes.text: Around a year before Volkswagen bought Bugatti, Piech sketched an eighteen-cylinder engine on an envelope while riding a Japanese express train. In nineteen ninety-eight, Volkswagen bought the Bugatti name for an estimated fifty million dollars. It got only the trademark.
scenes.caption: A SKETCH ON A TRAIN

scenes.text: Bugatti then showed a series of concept cars, all powered by a six point two five liter W18 engine with about five hundred fifty-five horsepower. The E B one eighteen, the E B two eighteen, and at the Frankfurt Motor Show in nineteen ninety-nine, a car called the eighteen slash three Chiron.
scenes.caption: THE FIRST CHIRON, 1999

scenes.text: So the name Chiron was used for a Bugatti concept seventeen years before the production Chiron arrived. Then came the E B eighteen slash four Veyron at the Tokyo show, almost identical to the car that would reach production. At Geneva in two thousand, Piech promised more than one thousand horsepower and more than four hundred kilometers per hour.
scenes.caption: THE PROMISE: 1,000 HP, 400 KM/H

scenes.text: The engine lost two cylinders and became the quad-turbo eight-liter W16. Top Gear wrote that the engine was not even the hardest part. The gearbox, the tires, and the aerodynamics were harder. Development took years and enormous sums of money.
scenes.caption: THE W16 IS BORN

scenes.text: Assembly of the Veyron began in September twenty oh five, in a new Molsheim factory. Bugatti was back home in Alsace. The car had one thousand one metric horsepower, and in twenty ten a Veyron sixteen point four Super Sport reached four hundred thirty-one kilometers per hour.
scenes.caption: BACK IN MOLSHEIM, 2005

scenes.text: But in twenty thirteen, evo reported an estimate from analysts at Sanford C. Bernstein. Volkswagen had lost about three point nine million pounds on every Veyron sold, and about one point four three billion pounds in total. The last Veyron was sold in February twenty fifteen.
scenes.caption: £3.9 MILLION LOST PER CAR

scenes.text: So the Chiron's mission was impossible on paper. It had to be faster than a car that had already broken records. It had to be more powerful, more usable, and more profitable. And it had to keep the same basic engine idea, because the W16 was now the heart of the brand.
scenes.caption: AN IMPOSSIBLE BRIEF

scenes.text: The answer was revealed on the first of March twenty sixteen at the Geneva Motor Show. It was previewed by the Bugatti Vision Gran Turismo concept, a car first created for a video game, shown at Frankfurt in twenty fifteen. The design team was led by Achim Anscheidt.
scenes.caption: PREVIEWED BY A VIDEO GAME CAR

scenes.text: The Chiron kept the eight-liter W16 and its four turbochargers, but Motor Authority reported that almost every part was redesigned. Output rose to fifteen hundred metric horsepower, or one thousand four hundred seventy-nine horsepower, with one thousand six hundred newton meters of torque.
scenes.caption: 1,500 PS

scenes.text: The design was a team effort. Wikipedia credits Achim Anscheidt as head of design, with Frank Heyl, Sasha Selipanov, and Etienne Salome. The most famous design element is the C-shaped line on the side, a curve that runs from the roof down around the door. It became the signature of the car, the line people recognize from across a parking lot.
scenes.caption: THE C-LINE

scenes.text: Underneath, the engineers were fighting heat. Motor Authority reported that the engine generates more than three thousand horsepower worth of heat, so the Chiron has ten radiators, a water pump moving about eight hundred liters per minute, and more than sixty thousand liters of air flowing through the engine every minute at full power. Making the power was hard. Surviving it was harder.
scenes.caption: 10 RADIATORS

scenes.text: The Chiron also introduced a detail owners love. In normal driving, the car is limited to about three hundred eighty kilometers per hour. To unlock its full limit of four hundred twenty, the driver needs a special speed key. Even a car this powerful came with a lock on its top speed, mainly because of the limits of road tires.
scenes.caption: THE SPEED KEY

scenes.text: The price was two point four million euros, with a two hundred thousand euro deposit. And the plan was to build five hundred cars. The first three were delivered in March twenty seventeen, and by then the first two hundred were already sold.
scenes.caption: €2.4 MILLION, 500 CARS

scenes.text: Here is the twist. The car named after a Monaco racing hero was never built to win races. It was built to be the fastest, most luxurious way to cross a continent. Bugatti's racing past gave the name. Its future was speed and luxury.
scenes.caption: A RACING NAME, A ROAD CAR

scenes.text: In August twenty seventeen, Bugatti put Juan Pablo Montoya in a Chiron. Montoya had won the Monaco Grand Prix in Formula One and the Indianapolis five hundred twice. The test was zero to four hundred kilometers per hour and back to zero. He did it in forty-one point nine six seconds, without a helmet or racing suit, according to Bugatti.
scenes.caption: MONTOYA, 41.96 SECONDS

scenes.text: Bugatti's own press release adds more detail. Montoya reached four hundred twenty kilometers per hour that weekend and went past four hundred kilometers per hour seventeen times. His previous personal best had been four hundred seven kilometers per hour, in an IndyCar. The run was certified by S G S T U V Saar, and Bugatti president Wolfgang Durheimer said three hundred of the five hundred Chirons had already been sold.
scenes.caption: 17 TIMES OVER 400 KM/H

scenes.text: The car itself showed off a new trick. Under braking from four hundred kilometers per hour, the rear wing stood up to forty-nine degrees as an air brake, less than a second after Montoya hit the pedal. Bugatti said it added about nine hundred kilograms of downforce at the rear and helped the car slow at about two g. The Chiron was proving it could stop as hard as it could go.
scenes.caption: THE WING BECOMES A BRAKE

scenes.text: But a small Swedish company answered within weeks. Koenigsegg's Agera RS beat the Chiron's time by more than five seconds, and in November twenty seventeen it averaged two hundred seventy-seven point nine miles per hour on a closed highway in Nevada. Bugatti now had a rival that took records personally.
scenes.caption: KOENIGSEGG STRIKES BACK

scenes.text: Bugatti answered on the second of August twenty nineteen. At Ehra-Lessien in Germany, Andy Wallace drove a pre-production Chiron Super Sport three hundred plus to three hundred four point seven seven three miles per hour. It was the first time a near-production car broke three hundred miles per hour.
scenes.caption: 304.773 MPH

scenes.text: And then came the twist nobody expected. Bugatti president Stephan Winkelmann said the goal had been to be the first to reach three hundred miles per hour, and that Bugatti would now focus on other areas. The company that had defined the top speed war walked away from it, at the very top.
scenes.caption: BUGATTI WALKS AWAY

scenes.text: What came next was a new kind of Bugatti business. Instead of chasing speed, the company built rarer and rarer versions. Thirty Super Sport three hundred plus cars at three point five million euros. Sixty Pur Sports for handling. Twenty Chiron Noire cars as a tribute to the nineteen thirty-six Type fifty-seven S C.
scenes.caption: RARER AND RARER

scenes.text: Then the one-offs. La Voiture Noire, unveiled in twenty nineteen, was inspired by the lost Type fifty-seven S C Atlantic that belonged to Jean Bugatti, and Wikipedia says it was sold for about nine and a half million pounds. Then the Chiron Profilee, which sold at RM Sotheby's in February twenty twenty-three for nine million seven hundred ninety-two thousand five hundred euros.
scenes.caption: LA VOITURE NOIRE

scenes.text: Hagerty reported that the Profilee became the most valuable new car ever sold at auction. Think about the circle here. A Type fifty-seven toy inspired Piech to revive Bugatti. Decades later, a tribute to the Type fifty-seven became one of the most expensive new cars in the world.
scenes.caption: THE CIRCLE CLOSES

scenes.text: Before the end, there was one more symbol. In twenty eighteen, Lego and Bugatti built a full-size, drivable Chiron from more than one million Lego Technic pieces, powered by two thousand three hundred four small electric motors. It made an estimated five point four horsepower and reached about twenty kilometers per hour. A brand that started with a toy in a shop had become a toy itself.
scenes.caption: A TOY AGAIN

scenes.text: Bugatti sold out the Chiron by January twenty twenty-two. By then, it had also used the Chiron's foundations for other cars, like the Divo, built for corners, and the Centodieci, a tribute to the E B one ten from the Italian era. So even the bankrupt chapter of Bugatti's history was brought back, on top of a Volkswagen-era Chiron.
scenes.caption: A TRIBUTE TO THE EB110

scenes.text: The last base-spec Chiron was built in September twenty twenty-three. In January twenty twenty-four, Motor1 reported the delivery of the last fifteen hundred metric horsepower Chiron to a Canadian buyer. And in May twenty twenty-four, the five hundredth and final Chiron left Molsheim.
scenes.caption: THE LAST CHIRONS

scenes.text: It was a Super Sport called L'Ultime. Top Gear reported that its two-tone blue paint recalls the first Chiron of twenty sixteen, and its sides list places from the car's story. Geneva, Paul Ricard, Ehra-Lessien, Molsheim. The number five hundred is engraved on the engine cover.
scenes.caption: L'ULTIME: No. 500

scenes.text: Two of the places on that livery tell a story of their own. Chateau Saint Jean and Cape Canaveral are listed by Top Gear as the sites of customer top speed runs. In other words, owners took their Chirons to private roads and to a former space launch area to reach the limit. Bugatti put those places on its last car as part of the Chiron's history.
scenes.caption: CAPE CANAVERAL

scenes.text: The W16 did not disappear at once. It lived on in the Bolide track car and the open Mistral. But the Chiron was the last main Bugatti built around it. One engine idea, born on an envelope on a train, powered the brand for almost two decades.
scenes.caption: THE W16'S LAST CHAPTER

scenes.text: Meanwhile, the company changed hands again. In twenty twenty-one, Volkswagen moved Bugatti into a joint venture with Rimac, the Croatian electric hypercar maker founded by Mate Rimac. Rimac held fifty-five percent, and Porsche forty-five.
scenes.caption: BUGATTI RIMAC, 2021

scenes.text: In June twenty twenty-four, the new company revealed the Chiron's successor, the Tourbillon. It uses a naturally aspirated eight point three liter V16 developed with Cosworth, plus three electric motors, for about one thousand seven hundred seventy-five horsepower. Its price is about three point eight million euros before taxes.
scenes.caption: THE TOURBILLON

scenes.text: And then, in September twenty twenty-six, Carscoops reported that a group of investors had bought Porsche's stakes in both Rimac and Bugatti Rimac. Volkswagen and Porsche now own nothing of Bugatti. Mate Rimac became Bugatti's president, and Porsche earned about one billion euros from the deal.
scenes.caption: VW IS OUT, 2026

scenes.text: Here is the final twist. Volkswagen bought Bugatti in nineteen ninety-eight for just the name, and turned it into the most famous hypercar brand in the world. Twenty-eight years later, it walked away completely. The Chiron was the peak of that era, the car that made the Volkswagen-era Bugatti a real business.
scenes.caption: THE PEAK OF AN ERA

scenes.text: So the story behind the Chiron is not only about horsepower. It is about a brand that died twice and came back three times. From Ettore in Molsheim, to Artioli in Italy, to Piech and his toy car, and now to Mate Rimac.
scenes.caption: DIED TWICE, BACK THREE TIMES

scenes.text: And it is about names. The Veyron carries the name of a Le Mans winner. The Chiron carries the name of the oldest man to start a Formula One race, a Monaco hero who won in Bugattis. Every modern Bugatti is a reminder of the brand's racing past, even if it no longer races.
scenes.caption: NAMED AFTER RACERS

scenes.text: Tell us in the comments which part of this story surprised you most. And watch the other videos in this Chiron series, two facts most people don't know, how it compares with the Koenigsegg Jesko, and what it really costs to own one.
scenes.caption: WHICH PART SURPRISED YOU?

scenes.text: If you are shopping for something more practical than a Bugatti, our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description. Subscribe to Pickup Reality for more stories about the machines people really talk about.
